In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chromatic number of the graph of a given distance set D is the smallest integer k for which D can be partitioned into k subsets D 1,..., D k such that the sum of the squares of the distances between any two points in the same subset is at most the sum of the square of the distances between points in different subsets.
the circular chromatic number of a graph G is the smallest number k such that the vertices of G can be assigned k different colors in such a way that every vertex has a neighbor of every color.
the fractional chromatic number is the best upper bound for the chromatic number of a graph, but the chromatic number is not always equal to the fractional chromatic.
